newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares overcome 1300 hurdle, gain 1.69pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares overcome 1300 hurdle, gain 1.69pct.

text.p: Strong buying interest propelled Greek equities through the 1,300 resistance level in yet another bullish session. Banks led the benchmark share index 1.69 percent higher on heavy volume of 22.8 billion drachmas.

"The trend is your best friend, stocks are continuing to look strong. We have a liquidity-driven market with falling interest rates prompting investors to get into equities," said Alexander Moraitakis, managing director at Nuntius Securities.
Fixed-income investors, long accustomed to attractive yields, are now realising that returns on government debt paper are quite lower while earned interest is also taxed, he said.
This had led to a reappraisal and a reallocation of portfolios into equities.

"Also, the Simitis administration is not yielding to repeated higher wage demands and the market seems to like this. There is a feeling that the economy's convergence effort has higher chances of approaching goals. This is the scenario that's driving shares higher," he said.
Bank shares led the climb on Thursday with gains of 3.45 percent. Construction firmed 0.41 percent with industrials closing 0.56 percent higher. Small-caps edged 0.27 percent hiogher.

The Bank of Greece said the country's current account deficit during January-October 1996 period widened 41 percent to $4.31 billion, reflecting a larger trade deficit and a smaller invisibles surplus.
Greece's foreign exchange reserves hit $20.5 billion drachmas at the end of January 1997, the central bank said.
The Athens general share index settled 1.69 percent or 21.65 points higher at 1306.46 points from Wednesday's 1284.81, after opening at 1288.13. The session's high was at 1308.02 points.
Turnover rose to 22.8 billion drachmas on volume of 6.6 million shares.
